title: DXF AAMA export loses annotations
content:
I'm trying to export in DXF format for use in Gerber and if I export a graded pattern, it grades on the sewing lines instead of the seam allowance. I can export individually (what a pain) but the annotations do not stay connected to the patterns. They are off in space. Now I'm stuck with a lot of patterns made for a client which I can't make in a format they can use, help.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Is your client using the Gerber Data Exchange Utility and selecting the "Grade on Sew Line" option during import? Since CLO anchors grading to the sewing line, this setting is required for Gerber to correctly read the nest and maintain the seam allowances, which are preserved as distinct coordinate data within the DXF-AAMA file.If this doesn't resolve the issue, please upload the file to our technical support portal for a deeper look: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/e53750502b674a94a09412ea375f6619

Comment 2: So, this is all in the CLO zpri file. It also doesn't show the seam allowance graded here, but when I switch sizes it shows the correct seam allowance so I know the data is there.

Comment 3: Hi carfritsch,Happy to help! Could you attach screenshots of your export settings, and the 2d window showing the patterns with seam allowance with grading on and off?
content_description: This page provides solutions for exporting graded sewing patterns in DXF format with correct seam allowance grading and properly attached annotations for use in Gerber systems.

title: Game Inspired Character Outfit — Recreated in Marvelous Designer
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/69f213cd187f4c0284ba3e11354e4c07INVISIB_19.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/23f5f0319f4b4022bb76e1f0681a751bINVISIB_19.png)Invisible Women Inspired Outfit — Marvelous Designer Project

While playing a game, I came across a character skin that immediately caught my attention because of its **bold colors, retro style, and strong character personality**. The design felt unique and stylish, and I wanted to challenge myself by recreating a similar outfit using **Marvelous Designer**.

This project became an opportunity to explore how a **game-inspired costume** could be translated into a garment created entirely through digital pattern making and cloth simulation.

![7fb2b8776aac4e388b6a4f5364ff9f15](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/7fb2b8776aac4e388b6a4f5364ff9f15Screenshot%20%28505%29.png)

* * *

### Reference and Inspiration

The main inspiration for this outfit came from Marvel Rivals **game character skin**. What stood out to me the most was the combination of:

  * Bright pink color palette

  * Retro fashion elements

  * Futuristic character styling




The design balances **playful fashion with a confident hero-like presence** , which made it an interesting challenge to recreate.

### Building the Outfit in Marvelous Designer

The outfit was constructed step by step inside Marvelous Designer using pattern-based garment creation.

The process started with the **base pants and top** , carefully fitted to the avatar to establish a clean silhouette. Once the foundation was working correctly, additional pieces were layered to build the final look.

Key garment pieces include:

  * A **structured corset-style top** with panel segmentation

  * **High-waisted pants** with curved seam lines

  * A **short cropped jacket** to add structure and contrast

  * A **scarf accessory** to introduce movement to the design




Each piece was simulated and adjusted to maintain a natural garment flow.

![64ee918a73394cb6afdda3267fefd00b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/64ee918a73394cb6afdda3267fefd00bScreenshot%20%28534%29.png)

### Details and Character Elements

To capture the personality of the original inspiration, several stylistic elements were incorporated:

  * A decorative **belt with circular details and emblem**

  * Retro-inspired **sunglasses**

  * Flowing lower pant sections that soften the silhouette




These elements help create a design that feels **stylish, playful, and character-driven**.

![f5f69c5af6474e519f90fba738533238](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/f5f69c5af6474e519f90fba738533238INVISIB_19.png)

![606c628ae36340e886989db582082cca](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/606c628ae36340e886989db582082ccaINVISIB_21.png)

### Final Thoughts

This project was mainly a **practice and exploration piece** , inspired by a game skin that I enjoyed while playing. Recreating it in Marvelous Designer helped me better understand **pattern construction, garment layering, and digital clothing simulation**.

It was a fun challenge to translate a **stylized game costume into a simulated garment** , and it allowed me to experiment with both **fashion design and character outfit creation**.

Reply 1: That’s such a compliment, thanks😍
content_description: Showcasing the digital recreation of a bold, retro-inspired game character outfit crafted step-by-step using Marvelous Designer for pattern making and cloth simulation.

title: DXF And PDF Files Imported To Clo3D Do Not Work
content:
DXF And PDF Files Imported To Clo3D Do Not Work

I exported those file from Affinity Designer (Vector Drawing App)

then imported into Clo3D with these methods with default settings.

File - Import - Adobe

File - Import - DXF (It does not open this file at all. It is greyed out.)

Original file looks like this.

![5cbcd3b011174f7186ccbc87d9e53407](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/0e9416cd35894620944b04a55f00315d/images/5cbcd3b011174f7186ccbc87d9e53407Screenshot%202026-03-11%20at%2019.11.21.png)

and when I import them into Clo3D looks like these.

![dc3fdee1bfdb42e7a5e76e7e56787f0c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/0e9416cd35894620944b04a55f00315d/images/dc3fdee1bfdb42e7a5e76e7e56787f0cScreenshot%202026-03-11%20at%2019.15.09.png)

So It definitely does not work at all.

How can I do these?

Affinity Designer File

[https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/mnx9a4es4kknidja8cjmt/Affinity-Designer-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.af?rlkey=c7kckskc5nolvhwzz6mbhnu7r&st=jpkcesam&dl=0](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/mnx9a4es4kknidja8cjmt/Affinity-Designer-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.af?rlkey=c7kckskc5nolvhwzz6mbhnu7r&st=jpkcesam&dl=0)

Exported PDF File

[https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/xkunqtxr8tffijjksunqi/Exported-PDF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.pdf?rlkey=nbhy8dbl57u0bpjhsi5vreqx1&st=blrq81ba&dl=0](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/xkunqtxr8tffijjksunqi/Exported-PDF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.pdf?rlkey=nbhy8dbl57u0bpjhsi5vreqx1&st=blrq81ba&dl=0)

Exported DXF File

[https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/f5olc7l2455fxq89gquit/Exported-DXF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing?rlkey=0p10csccn04gh0yjukopyxwcg&st=50gjue8x&dl=0](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/f5olc7l2455fxq89gquit/Exported-DXF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing?rlkey=0p10csccn04gh0yjukopyxwcg&st=50gjue8x&dl=0)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Why DXF is Greyed Out:The file is missing the .dxf extension in your folder. Manually rename the file to include .dxf at the end. CLO 3D won't let you select it otherwise.Not seeing patterns (Join Points):CLO is struggling to interpret your file because your pant outlines are broken segments. In Affinity, select all lines forming the pant perimeter and use Layer > Geometry > Merge (or Join Curves) to create one continuous, closed loop.Clean the File:Delete all text and numbers (1, 5, 23, "ÖN", etc.) before exporting. CLO tries to turn every single digit into a separate pattern piece, which causes the "mess" and circles you see.If Affinity DXF still doesn't work:Affinity cannot export apparel-standard DXFs (AAMA/ASTM). If you have trouble importing Affinity's standard DXF, you are probably better off exporting as PDF (Digital - High Quality) from Affinity.
Reply 1: It works now. Thank you very much.
content_description: This page aims to identify and resolve issues with importing DXF and PDF files exported from Affinity Designer into Clo3D, ensuring proper file compatibility and workflow.
